text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: GLB alert — observed sustained GPU pool saturation in eu-west-1 (avg 92% for 5m). Autothrottle kicked in for some model variants.

maya: saw that, we're getting OOM errors on some 80GB pools. nice catch by monitoring.

ben: is autothrottle just lowering weights or doing hard cutoffs?

infra-bot: autothrottle lowers route weight by up to 30% then triggers fallback routing to compatible model variants in other regions. No hard node evictions.

maya: want to avoid a big cross-region spike to na-west. Can we do a gradual steer using weighted gradient?

sandeep: +1. Recommend a staged weight change: 10% -> 20% -> 35% over 10m windows, watch tail latency. Also lower max-burst for eu-west to cap retries.

evan: current GLB policy is `latency-first, cost-aware` with region-preference: eu, na. I can push a temporary policy override to `balanced` to favor na slightly.

jo: prefer explicit command so it's auditable. evan — can you paste the command you'll run?

evan: running locally to test, plan to run:```
redwoodctl glb update --policy staged-weight --from eu-west-1 --to na-west-1 --steps "10,20,35" --step-interval 300 --meta "incident/1765439876"
```

ben: what about dedicated clusters pinned to eu? Those won't failover automatically. We need a capacity check for dedicated tenants before shifting.

maya: good call. I'll run a quick query: `SELECT pool, free_gpus FROM capacity WHERE region='na-west-1' AND gpu_type='H100'` and share counts.

(maya posts)
```
pool-a: free_gpus=18
pool-b: free_gpus=7 (maintenance window in 2h)
pool-c: free_gpus=42
```

sandeep: na-west has headroom but pool-b maintenance reduces effective capacity. We should exclude pool-b in the immediate steering.

evan: updated plan: steer to na-west-1 pools [pool-a, pool-c] only. Command:```
redwoodctl glb update --policy staged-weight --from eu-west-1 --to na-west-1 --target-pools "pool-a,pool-c" --steps "10,20,35" --step-interval 300 --meta "incident/1765439876"
```

jo: please also enable prefix/KV cache warmup in na-west for the most common model IDs to avoid cold starts.

ben: telemetry alert knobs? We should create short-lived monitors for: token latency p95, retry rate, and cost per token delta.

maya: creating monitors now.

infra-bot: monitor created: `incident-1765439876-p95-latency`, `incident-1765439876-retries`, `incident-1765439876-cost-delta`. Alerts at 15% degradation.

evan: executing staged update now (step 1 -> 10%). Will report after 2m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

(maya) :thumbsup: watching logs.

2m later — evan: step 1 complete. na-west p95 latency +3%, retries +1. no errors. continuing to step 2.

ben: reminder: track token cost delta. If cost > 25% we revert to partial weight restore and fallback to model quantized variant to save GPU cycles.

sandeep: second step done (20%). small spike in tail latency for legacy model v1.1, rolled those requests to quantized v1.1-q by rule.

maya: third step (35%) in progress.

evan: final step done. overall traffic shifted. eu-west GPU saturation dropped to 48% after shift. na-west p95 up 6% but within SLO for most routes.

jo: add note to runbook: when doing staged GLB steering, exclude pools under maintenance and pre-warm KV cache in target pools.

maya: filing a quick post-incident doc. tagging owners for follow-up on dedicated tenant placement.

ben: :white_check_mark: good run. leave the staged policy in place for 30m then revert to normal routing.

infra-bot: note: scheduled revert at +30m unless a manual override occurs.

evan: logging the exact commands and outputs to incident ticket #INC-2026-312.

jo: thanks everyone. great coordination. :clap:
